{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABYgdsuw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhCE4Eo", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 9, "title": "Redesign the playable web emulator into a minimal, game-first player UI", "body": "## Problem

The browser emulator is now capable of running the original **Beacon Trail** ROM, but its presentation still looks like a developer demo rather than a polished game player. The current `web/index.html` puts multiple explanatory paragraphs, a conventional fieldset, ROM/status messages, and a lengthy control guide **before and after** a relatively small canvas. `web/src/style.css` provides almost no visual hierarchy, layout system, or responsive treatment.

Someone who visits [the public player](https://takahirox.github.io/wonderswan-rust/) should immediately see the game screen and be able to start playing, without reading hardware/implementation explanations. Developers should still be able to find technical information on demand.

## Expected outcome

Redesign the existing browser frontend as a **modern, minimal, dark-themed, game-first player**, with a restrained accent inspired by SwanCrystal hardware. Use these references for *interaction and layout ideas*, **not** copied code/visual assets:

- [Afterplay](https://afterplay.io/) — uncluttered, polished game-player presentation.
- [webЯcade](https://play.webrcade.com/) — game-first layout and controls that are revealed when needed.
- [EmulatorJS](https://demo.emulatorjs.org/) — separating advanced options and debugging from the main player.

The result should have **three information layers**:

1. **Normal player (default):** a prominently sized 224×144 game viewport, a compact product/ROM title, an easily discoverable **Play demo** call-to-action when no ROM is loaded, visible/selectable console model (default **SwanCrystal**), and concise **Pause/Resume**, **Restart**, **Fullscreen**, **Load ROM**, and **Settings/Help** actions. No multi-paragraph emulator/hardware description in this view.
2. **Settings / Help (on demand):** short keyboard-control instructions, the current limited-compatibility notice, demo download/source/license links, and the Debug Mode toggle. Keep ROM loading discoverable from the normal player; it may also be available in settings.
3. **Debug Mode (explicit opt-in, off by default):** a collapsible side panel on larger screens and a responsive drawer/section on smaller screens. Show only **real, available** machine/UI diagnostics (e.g., active model, ROM name and byte count, running/paused/stopped state, measured/rendered FPS or frame count if properly instrumented, execution errors). Do not invent CPU registers or pretend accuracy metrics are available; adding full CPU-debugger APIs is **not** required.

**Primary principle:** keep the game canvas visually dominant. The normal view must remain usable with no debug panel open.

## Context and implementation guidance

Relevant existing files:
- `web/index.html` currently renders descriptions, a `fieldset#controls`, model select, `#demo`, `#pause`, `#reset`, local `#rom` input, status paragraphs, `#error`, and `canvas#screen`.
- `web/src/main.ts` already initializes Rust/Wasm, fetches the CC0 demo, loads local ROM bytes, handles model switching, pause/resume, restart, keyboard mappings, focus, and visibility changes.
- `web/src/style.css` is intentionally minimal. `web/scripts` already contains browser smoke-test tooling. Inspect the latest state before editing and adapt tests as necessary.
- Build/deploy: `npm run build:wasm`, `npm run build`, and the existing GitHub Pages workflow; production base is `/wonderswan-rust/`.
- Preserve the repository's [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), [review guidance](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md), and [Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md), including English collaboration and honest validation reporting.

### Visual direction

- Use a small, consistent palette: near-black/charcoal page and player chrome, off-white text, muted gray secondary text, and **one** subtle SwanCrystal-inspired accent. Prefer restrained borders, spacing, and typography over decorative effects, fake hardware textures, or bright gradients.
- Center the player in a comfortable max-width container. Make the screen the strongest element above the fold on a typical desktop (e.g., 1440×900), with appropriately grouped, consistently sized controls immediately around it. A compact branded header and the game title are enough.
- Maintain the canvas **internal resolution 224×144**, its exact aspect ratio, nearest-neighbor/pixelated scaling, and crisp pixels at all layouts, including fullscreen. Do not distort/crop the output. A visually framed screen is fine but avoid a large fake console shell.
- Use short labels and recognizable icons **with accessible names**, visible hover/focus/disabled/active states, and sufficient contrast. Icons must not be the only cue for an important error or unfamiliar action.
- Avoid mandatory splash screens, animated intros, marketing sections, ROM-library/catalog UI, an additional visual-design framework, or unnecessary dependencies.

### Functional and responsive UX

- **Empty/loading state:** show an obvious Play demo action and a smaller Load ROM alternative; while Wasm initializes, show a calm loading state; show actionable, human-readable error feedback if initialization or ROM loading fails. Preserve recovery after an invalid ROM.
- **Playing state:** prioritize the viewport; show concise ROM title and play/pause state, with Pause/Resume, Restart, Fullscreen, console-model selector, and a route to Settings/Help. Preserve all existing emulator behaviors and constraints.
- **Model switch:** allow exactly WonderSwan (mono), WonderSwan Color, and SwanCrystal (default); switching should restart the current cartridge as it does now. Communicate this briefly near the selector or in a concise tooltip/help, rather than a permanent paragraph.
- **Keyboard:** keep existing Arrow/WASD movement, Z/X A/B, and Enter Start/restart bindings. Opening dialogs/menus, moving focus, and typing/selecting must not cause the game to receive input; clear held keys when focus is lost or an overlay opens. Restore focus sensibly when returning to the game.
- **Help and Settings:** implement using ordinary accessible controls/dialog behavior (focus entry/return, Escape to close, and no keyboard-focus traps outside the active dialog). When a modal settings/help panel opens, pause if playing; closing it should restore the previous running state only when appropriate, and must not automatically resume a tab that was background-paused.
- **Debug Mode:** opt-in from Settings, off on page load; closing or disabling it returns the player to the clean presentation. Diagnostics update without disrupting frame execution; avoid high-frequency DOM updates that introduce unnecessary work.
- **Fullscreen:** a visible, working control for supported browsers, using Fullscreen API with appropriate graceful handling on unsupported/failed attempts. Aspect ratio and pixelated rendering must remain correct.
- **Mobile/narrow widths:** ensure the screen and primary controls remain usable without horizontal scrolling or overlapping controls around 375px viewport width. Provide a minimal **touch controller** for mobile (directional input, A, B, Start), wired into the existing emulated keypad; support holding/releasing buttons, release on pointer cancel/blur, and avoid page scroll while interacting with these controls. Do not duplicate game logic in JavaScript.
- **Accessibility:** semantic controls and labels, visible focus indicators, readable text and contrast, usable keyboard navigation, announcements for important load/execution errors without noisy repeated announcements, and touch targets of a practical size.
- Preserve original ROM/license links somewhere reachable from Settings/Help; keep copyright provenance explicit even though verbose descriptions leave the default screen. ROM loading remains local-only with no upload endpoint.
- Keep existing TypeScript + HTML + CSS architecture unless the current code shows a concrete reason to change. This is a **frontend UX redesign**, not an emulator-core feature Issue.

### Suggested player structure (illustrative, not a demand for exact markup)

```text
WONDER/SWAN                                 [SwanCrystal ▾]
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  224 × 144 game                      │
│                 (large, centered)                    │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
Beacon Trail                         [Pause] [Restart] [⛶] [⚙]
[Load ROM]                                     [? Controls]

Settings / Help (hidden by default): controls, compatibility, ROM/license,
Debug Mode switch.
Debug Mode (hidden by default): actual runtime diagnostics.
Touch controls: appear on touch/mobile layout, not on desktop by default.
```

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] On a fresh page load, the normal view is a **game-first dark player**, with the 224×144 canvas visually dominant, a visible default SwanCrystal model selector, a prominent Play demo action when idle, and concise playback/ROM/settings controls. Hardware explanations and debug data are **not** shown by default.
- [ ] All three console choices work and retain their existing semantics; the playable original Beacon Trail ROM can be started, paused/resumed, restarted, completed, and played again. Loading the local demo ROM still works; invalid ROMs show a recoverable error; user ROM bytes stay in-browser.
- [ ] Settings/Help exposes short, accurate instructions and compatibility limitations, plus links to the original demo ROM, its source, and CC0 license/provenance. Settings can be opened and closed via pointer and keyboard, including Escape; game input is suspended while interacting with it.
- [ ] The Debug Mode switch is **off by default**. When enabled, a panel displays factual model/ROM/execution information available from the current implementation; disabling it removes developer-only UI. No fabricated CPU, memory, or performance values.
- [ ] Fullscreen works where supported, and returns to the normal layout on exit. Failure/unsupported cases do not break playback and are communicated appropriately.
- [ ] On desktop (e.g., 1440×900) and narrow/mobile viewports (e.g., 375×812), the canvas preserves its 224:144 ratio and crisp pixel output; the layout has no horizontal overflow, clipped controls, or obstructive permanent help text. Primary actions remain discoverable.
- [ ] On touch/mobile, on-screen direction/A/B/Start buttons actually affect the emulated game and can be held/released without stuck inputs. Keyboard inputs remain functional on desktop, and focus/menu interactions do not send unintended gameplay input.
- [ ] Loading, paused, running, empty, and error states are visibly distinguishable without requiring Debug Mode. Important errors remain accessible while verbose technical details stay hidden.
- [ ] Maintain existing emulator logic, current build scripts, local behavior, and GitHub Pages `/wonderswan-rust/` asset path. Do not introduce ROM uploads, copyrighted bundled ROMs, unrelated game features, or speculative dependencies.
- [ ] Extend/update the existing automated browser smoke tests for the new interface and regression paths: demo play-through and restart, model switch, local ROM load/error, settings/help toggle, Debug Mode default/on/off, fullscreen where available, keyboard/focus behavior, and mobile touch controls. Existing Rust tests, Wasm compilation, and frontend production build pass; report actual results.
- [ ] Review the rendered UI at **desktop and narrow viewport sizes** (screenshots or equivalent browser inspection) before merge for hierarchy, spacing, legibility, and control access. Summarize observed issues/fixes in the PR; this is an implementer-performable check, not an unspecified subjective human approval requirement.
- [ ] Update only necessary frontend documentation so controls/settings and debug behavior are accurately described; report limitations honestly.

## Optional validation

- Check additional desktop/mobile browsers and a real touch device if available. Report observations but do not make hardware ownership a prerequisite.
- Perform a brief visual comparison against the referenced players to identify polish improvements, without copying their imagery or markup.

## Required post-merge verification

1. **Pending:** Confirm the existing GitHub Pages workflow succeeds for the merge commit on `main`; record the run URL and outcome.
2. **Pending:** Open the public URL without authentication and verify the new player, bundled demo, model selection, menu and Debug Mode behavior, ROM links, and key assets in production. Note any deployment-only defects.

Production deployment checks occur **after** merge and are not pre-merge approval requirements.
